Operations Transformation

Get a stalled transformation moving again.

Transformation rarely fails because there is not enough activity. It fails when ownership and daily operating behaviour never change. Milestones turn green while the operation carries on as before.

Warning signs

  • The programme reports progress, but operating KPIs have not moved.
  • Key decisions wait for one or two people.
  • Teams see the change as something done to them.
  • Nobody can say who will own the new process after go-live.

How I help

I review the programme against what is happening on the floor. I test whether the original case still holds, find where ownership has slipped, and rebuild the governance and routines that carry the change into daily operation.

What changes

  • An honest assessment of where the programme stands
  • A reset plan with clear owners, decision gates and measures
  • A daily, weekly and monthly operating rhythm
  • A handover plan so the change does not depend on me

Relevant evidence

Continuous improvement maturity rose from 1.27 to 2.0 within 12 months on the business’s internal assessment, with savings above the previous three years combined. Colleague engagement rose from 64 to 71.

Questions

Can you lead the programme directly?

Yes. I can work as an adviser, a programme lead or an interim leader.

What if the business case no longer holds?

Then I will say so. Pausing a programme is sometimes the right call.
